content:
jamal.support: FYI customer (acme_ops) reporting intermittent 504s and very high tail latency hitting hosted inference. Started ~15:12 UTC. :rotating_light:
acme_ops: We're getting 504s from the Redwood API regularly. P95 is fine but P99/P999 spike to 8-12s then 504. This is breaking our UI.
jamal.support: Logged a support ticket and escalated to SRE/runtime. Customer says volume hasn't changed on their side. They provided a short repro curl.
acme_ops: repro: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"model":"rwd-compat-medium","input":"hello"}' --repeat 100 concurrent 5
sarah.oncall: seeing the alert: gateway_5xx_rate up and queue_depth high on hosted-gateway in eu-west. Investigating.
ingress-bot: [ALERT] hosted-gateway/eu-west queue_depth=1980 (limit=2000) p99_latency=9.6s continuous_batching_backlog=220 batches_pending=12
kai.runtime: pinging in — continuous batching backlog + queue depth indicates requests are piling up waiting for KV/cache or batch formation. Could be a small subset of requests with long seq_len or some clients using very large context.
emily.product: customer says they didn't change context length. They use previews with images sometimes; maybe a model variant mismatch?
sarah.oncall: I pulled metrics: top tenant by requests is acme_ops but their avg tokens per request are normal. However we have a stuck batcher worker on host gpu-23 showing repeated "awaiting KV dump" logs.
kai.runtime: can you paste the logs?
sarah.oncall: ```
2026-03-15T15:14:02Z batcher[gpu-23]: enqueue req tenant=acme_ops req_id=abcd path=/generate tokens=128
2026-03-15T15:14:04Z batcher[gpu-23]: batch_form_time=312ms kv_cache_lock wait=280ms
2026-03-15T15:14:04Z batcher[gpu-23]: dispatch delayed; backlog_queue_len=68
2026-03-15T15:14:07Z runtime[gpu-23]: error fetching KV for model=rwd-compat-medium shard=3 timeout
2026-03-15T15:14:07Z batcher[gpu-23]: p99_latency=9.2s
```
kai.runtime: That KV timeout looks like a clear culprit — one shard having IO stalls causes batch assembly to block and subsequent requests pile up in the gateway queue. Continuous batching wants to wait to form bigger batches, so tail latency increases.
jamal.support: Customer says this is causing intermittent user-facing errors; wants ETA.
sarah.oncall: Immediate mitigations I can do: 1) drain the problematic host (gpu-23) from serving pool 2) set gateway queue_limit to 1600 to trigger earlier backpressure 3) reduce max_batch_delay_ms from 30 -> 10 to force smaller batches so backlog doesn't accumulate. Which should we apply first?
kai.runtime: Drain gpu-23 first. Then do reduced batch_delay as temporary. Queue_limit change safer to avoid hitting global limit and triggering more 5xx.
emily.product: If we reduce batch_delay, cost might go up but customer uptime matters. Also consider automatic fallback to a smaller/less-sharded model for this tenant while we remediate.
jamal.support: I'll get acme_ops on a short maintenance window for fallback to rwd-compat-small.
acme_ops: we prefer minimal changes — fallback OK for 30 minutes. Please advise when done.
sarah.oncall: Performing drain now. ```/bin/curl -X POST https://ops-api/inventory/drain -d '{"host":"gpu-23"}'```
ingress-bot: [INFO] drain started host=gpu-23; active_sessions=12; not accepting new sessions
sarah.oncall: Changing max_batch_delay_ms on eu-west batcher config from 30 to 10 and increasing queue_prune_threshold so early-reject engages at 85% instead of 95%. Applying now.```
opsctl set-config --region eu-west --service batcher --set max_batch_delay_ms=10 --set early_reject_threshold=0.85
```
kai.runtime: Confirmed config pushed. Watching now.
ingress-bot: [METRICS] queue_depth=1200 -> 900 (3m after); p99_latency=9.6s -> 2.1s; continuous_batching_backlog=220 -> 40
sarah.oncall: Also scaled up dedicated worker pool for rwd-compat-medium by +2 replicas while draining to help capacity.
akai.error: (developer note) reduced batch_delay will increase total compute but reduces tail.
jamal.support: Told customer we'll fallback them to rwd-compat-small now while we watch.
acme_ops: Thanks — latency improved on our side, saw no 504s in the last 3 minutes. We appreciate quick action.
emily.product: Follow-ups: 1) root cause likely KV shard IO flakiness on gpu-23 — file a runtime bug 2) add an automated playbook step for 'KV timeout -> drain host + reduce batch_delay' 3) check tenant routing so single-tenant hot spots don't overload one shard.
kai.runtime: Agree. I'll open a Jira (RWD-OPS-11234) with logs and plan for adding shard health checks + per-tenant shard isolation as mitigation.
sarah.oncall: Last: re-enable original batch_delay after verification window (30m) and return queued config to nominal. I'll keep monitoring for 1h.
jamal.support: Customer updated ticket: "service recovered, will monitor" — marking P1 -> P2.
acme_ops: appreciate the fast turnaround.
jamal.support: Closing loop: actions taken: drained gpu-23; reduced max_batch_delay_ms; increased early_reject_threshold; scaled up worker pool; customer fallback temporary. Next steps assigned to kai.runtime for hardening.
emily.product: I'll draft a postmortem with proposed product-level mitigations (per-tenant routing, rate-awareness, and smarter fallback policies).
ingress-bot: [CLOSE] incident 2112345678 transitioned to resolved-coordinating
